coverage_summary: Reviewed all eight trajectories. Most documented transformations and opaque model boundaries are supported, but the graph omits spatial-neighborhood segmentation, misbinds traversal order, loses optional-input branches, and misrepresents conversational fine-tuning/inference state and task branching.

findings.detail: The fine-tuning path starts from all cell sentences and sends them directly into traversal. The paper explicitly documents segmenting each tissue section into square L×L spatial neighborhoods before assembling one sentence per neighborhood.

evidence.quote: For each tissue section, we segmented the entire section into square regions of size L × L micrometers, referred to as spatial neighborhoods.
For each spatial neighborhood j , cells with their cell sentences { s i } n i =1 were assembled in pre-determined spatial order to construct one spatial sentence

findings.required_change: Add the documented section-to-spatial-neighborhood partition/selection and connect neighborhood-specific cell sentences to traversal and assembly; retain L×L as a source parameter.

findings.detail: The spatial assembly call binds traversal_order to the serialize operation's values port alongside cell_sentences. The paper describes σ as the traversal order controlling assembly, not as textual content being serialized.

evidence.quote: where σ = ( σ 1 , σ 2 , . . . , σ n ) denotes the traversal order of cells within the frame.
cells with their cell sentences { s i } n i =1 were assembled in pre-determined spatial order to construct one spatial sentence

findings.required_change: Pass cell sentences as the serialized values and represent traversal_order as the order/control parameter or an explicitly documented ordering port; do not treat it as another serialized value.

findings.detail: The cell serializer always receives cell_metadata despite the paper describing metadata as optional. No bypass or conditional serializer branch represents cells without metadata.

evidence.quote: where ( x i , y i ) denotes its spatial coordinates, m i represents optional metadata (e.g., cell type or spatial domain), and o i is the ranked gene sentence

findings.required_change: Represent metadata as a conditional input with a bypass for the absent-metadata case, or explicitly scope this trajectory to the metadata-present configuration.

findings.detail: The conditional-generation receipt treats target_cell_metadata as an unconditional required input, although metadata is optional in the documented framework.

evidence.quote: While the location of the cell and the information from neighboring cells are essential, TISSUENARRATOR can also condition on optional metadata such as cell type.
In the conditional generation mode, users can specify the target cell type or other metadata (e.g., tissue region or disease state)

findings.required_change: Add the metadata-present condition and an absent-metadata bypass, while retaining the neighboring-cell and target-location inputs as essential inputs.

findings.detail: The conversational fine-tuning trajectory is labeled as fine-tuning Qwen3-4B-Base directly and has no prior spatial-sentence-trained model state. The paper states that task-specific fine-tuning follows large-scale spatial-sentence training and fine-tunes TISSUENARRATOR.

evidence.quote: Following large-scale training on spatial sentences, TISSUENARRATOR can be fine-tuned on smaller, task-specific datasets to extend its functionality beyond cell generation.
We split the dataset by structure name, fine-tuned TISSUENARRATOR, and evaluated the model on questions derived from held-out structures.

findings.required_change: Record the spatial-sentence-trained TISSUENARRATOR state as the initialization/context for conversational Q&A fine-tuning, rather than presenting the route as a direct base-model fine-tune.

findings.detail: The inference trajectory invents a prepare_conversational_query transformation and maps qa_query to itself. The paper documents natural-language queries and held-out-structure evaluation, but no query-preparation operation.

evidence.quote: TISSUENARRATOR generalizes to unseen anatomical structure names in natural language queries
We split the dataset by structure name, fine-tuned TISSUENARRATOR, and evaluated the model on questions derived from held-out structures.

findings.required_change: Remove the unsupported preparation step or retain a direct opaque model-input boundary for the documented natural-language query.

findings.detail: The inference route presents top-five cell types, top-twenty genes, and description generation as three unconditional outputs from the same query. The paper defines these as distinct task types, so the graph needs task-specific conditions or an unresolved task-selection boundary.

evidence.quote: we constructed a proof-of-concept dataset covering three tasks: given the name of an anatomical structure, (1) return the top 5 most abundant cell types, (2) list the top 20 highly expressed genes, and (3) generate a natural-language description of the structure.
List the major cell classes present in the Dorsal peduncular area region from the mouse brain (include up to five).
Provide a concise scientific summary of the brain division 'cranial nerves' from the mouse brain. Describe its overall functional role and highlight representative structures and their significance.

findings.required_change: Mark the three outputs as mutually exclusive task branches with task-specific query conditions, or retain a single opaque conversational-Q&A boundary whose task selection is explicitly unresolved.

findings.detail: The held-out Q&A inference variant again identifies only a Qwen3-4B-Base model fine-tuned for Q&A, without preserving that inference uses the model after spatial-sentence training and subsequent task-specific fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: Following large-scale training on spatial sentences, TISSUENARRATOR can be fine-tuned on smaller, task-specific datasets to extend its functionality beyond cell generation.
We split the dataset by structure name, fine-tuned TISSUENARRATOR, and evaluated the model on questions derived from held-out structures.

findings.required_change: Identify the receiving model as the sequentially spatial-trained and Q&A-fine-tuned TISSUENARRATOR variant, preserving the preceding training state in the inference context.
